levels.title: How Do Games Work?
levels.blurb: it started with one question — how do people actually make video games? found Python, stayed up too late writing bad code, loved every second of it. that curiosity never really left.

levels.title: Hardware & Fundamentals
levels.blurb: started a bachelor's in IT. first real labs: taking apart computers, understanding networking, sysadmin fundamentals. learned to think from the ground up — what's physically happening, not just what the screen says.

levels.title: Networks & Systems
levels.blurb: deep in Packet Tracer, routing protocols, subnetting. building and breaking network topologies in labs. somewhere in here it clicked — i was more interested in what could go wrong than how to set things up.

levels.title: The FIU Transfer
levels.blurb: transferring to FIU was the biggest call i made for my career. went all-in on cybersecurity: got Security+, built a home lab with Kali Linux, started pen testing, blue teaming, and made HackTheBox a regular habit.

levels.title: First CCDC
levels.blurb: first CCDC as a participant. red team was relentless. i learned more in those 8 hours than in months of coursework. confirmed this is what i wanted to do.

levels.title: Lab Life
levels.blurb: got my first tech job — Hardware Lab Assistant at FIU. fell in love with it. managed the lab environment, tutored students in C and Java, ran hardware workshops. great team. the kind of job that makes you better at explaining anything.

levels.title: Cloud Discovery
levels.blurb: FIU offered a free AWS course — took it on a whim. went deep fast. cloud security clicked immediately. built projects, certified as AWS Solutions Architect. the hardware lab closed around the same time, so i moved on to a new chapter.

levels.title: First Authorship
levels.blurb: new role: Course Learning Assistant. mostly tutoring, until a professor offered to bring me into research — using AI to evaluate security requirement completeness. i said yes. ended up as first author on a submitted paper. didn't see that coming.

levels.title: CCDC Captain
levels.blurb: second CCDC, this time as captain. five people, one week of prep, 48 teams. placed 16th. held operations under constant red team pressure until the last minute.

levels.title: Everything Connects
levels.blurb: now i work where everything meets — cloud, security engineering, and AI. building systems that actually defend themselves. aiming to become a cloud architect. still just a really curious person who never stopped building.
